editorial_contributions.text: It is well known that a Möbius transformation maps circles to circles, less well known is the converse that a nonconstant meromorphic function on the Riemann sphere \({\mathbb{C}}_{\infty}\) which preserves circles must be a Möbius transformation. The author presents two strong local versions of this converse. For a function f meromorphic on a region \(D\subset {\mathbb{C}}_{\infty}\) and n a positive integer or infinity let \(A_ n\) denote the set of all \(z\in D\) such that there are at least n circular arcs (with distinct tangent lines) through z which are mapped into circular arcs by f. The author proves that if either \(A_ 3\) has an accumulation point in D or \(A_{\infty}\) has at least three points, then f is the restriction to D of a Mobius transformation. Both of these results are sharp. The main tools in the proofs of these results are the Schwarzian derivative and a formula which relates the rate of change of Euclidean curvature to the Schwarzian derivative. The author closes by asking whether similar results hold for smooth transformations acting on \({\mathbb{R}}^ n\).
